topic.intent: Implement runtime human takeover for a browser agent blocked on an interaction requiring an authorized person; preserve the live session, stop automation, verify completion, and resume from fresh state.

publicSignals.visibleSignal: Question asks how to handle a Browser Use automation that stops at CAPTCHA, 2FA or changed layouts, and asks about overnight failures. A commenter discusses a human takeover primitive.
publicSignals.relativeAgeAsDisplayed: question: 7mo ago; commenter: 7mo ago; update/comment: 6mo ago

publicSignals.visibleSignal: Issue title asks how to stop an agent to obtain required information from the user; issue opened 2025-11-22, references Browser Use 0.9.7, and is closed.
publicSignals.interpretation: Evidence that a related tool-calling question was raised, not current API advice; old issue version is explicitly not used as current implementation guidance.

primaryEvidence.supports: Current docs describe custom Python tools including human-in-the-loop and 2FA-related examples; tools are registered with @tools.action and receive documented typed parameters. Not a claim of a built-in universal takeover product.
Current docs show a custom ask_human function and emphasize exact browser_session parameter name and BrowserSession type for injected context.

Current upstream open-source docs describe Browser keep_alive lifecycle option and retained browser between tasks. This is not a guarantee that an owned Chrome process/page survives every Agent cleanup path; article cautions to check installed release and ownership.
Playwright debugging documentation describes page.pause/Inspector for headed interactive debugging; article distinguishes it from durable production handoff orchestration.

Authentication docs explain storage of authenticated state and warn that state files can contain cookies/headers usable to impersonate an account; supports source-control caution and distinction from current live page takeover.
